_doc: Klaude OSC display. Single source of truth for the avatar side (build.py -> shaders, layout, font atlas) and the client (kd package). Change a value, run build.py, then Setup2.All() in Unity. width/height = the screen (text coordinates); the graphics plane is width/gfx_scale x height/gfx_scale pixels. Animating material values costs ~n^2 per renderer per frame, so graphics memory is kept small and split over renderers.

screen._sizes_doc: screen sizes the avatar switches between at run time (register screen = index, +16 = low-resolution graphics: 2x2 px dots, a quarter of the data; Display.set_size(i, lowres)), all about 128x128 pixels in 16 px steps: 176x96 (chat), 128x128, 208x80, 160x112, 112x144, 96x176 (pictures pick the closest aspect). Memory and text header are sized for the largest; size_m = the width of a 128 px wide screen in metres (wider sizes are wider).

frame._doc: Frame around the screen (shader-drawn on the bezel quad, lit by the world): bezel_color = body, bezel_px = width in screen pixels (placement keeps the whole frame clear of the body). radius_px = outer corner radius; edge = thin outline; lip = recess around the screen; led = indicator dot in the bottom bezel (null = none).
frame.label: Klaude Display
frame._mascot_doc: Klawd (the mascot), left of the label on the top bar: o = body, e = eye, . = frame. Rows are doubled: in the terminal each half-block pixel is twice as tall as wide.
frame._anim_doc: Klawd walks in place: mascot / mascot_step alternate at walk_hz, the step frame 1 px higher (a bob); the eyes close for blink_s every blink_every_s seconds. Shader only (each viewer's own clock).

color._doc: bpp = graphics bits per pixel. 1: attribute colour (2 colours per 8x8 tile, 1 B per tile); 2: NES style (4 colours per tile, 2 B per tile). Each tile entry holds one 4-bit palette index per pixel value. Palette = 16 colours, sent as RGB565. Mono mode (register) maps every colour's luminance onto mono_bg..mono_fg.

sync._tiers_doc: Sync tiers of the avatar (KuraDot full / standard / lite; the Klaude avatar is full): a page of payload_bytes goes over the wire in chunks of tiers[tier] bytes. full = KD_P + KD_B0..29 (248 bits); standard = 2 chunks of 16 B (KD_P + KD_S0 + KD_B0..15, 137 bits); lite = 3 chunks of 10 B (KD_P + KD_S0..1 + KD_B0..9, 90 bits). Only the chunks that changed are sent.
sync._limits_doc: features a tier leaves out: hires false = pictures only in the low-resolution mode; wings n = at most n side screens open at once.
sync._refresh_doc: refresh = send every non-zero page again in turn (late joiners, lost frames; one-way OSC, the client never knows who joined) at refresh_rate_hz when idle (= rate_hz: idle frames are free); while new content keeps coming, every 1/refresh_busy_share-th frame is still a refresh frame, so nothing static ever starves. refresh_core_share of the refresh frames go to the core pages (palette, registers, sprite registers, text) so a late joiner sees text and the screen state within seconds; the rest walk the graphics pages.

_registers_doc: STATE registers (late joiners get them from the refresh like any page): flags 1 on, 2 invert, 4 graphics, 8 text, 16 mono, 32 photo dither, 64 sprites, 128 window | gfx_mode 0 raw 1 photo | gfx_x/gfx_y, text_x/text_y: layer offset in screen pixels (content moves by +offset, wraps; graphics at zoom 1 units) | mono fg<<4|bg | gfx_vx..text_vy: auto-scroll, signed px/s (TIME based: every viewer runs his own clock, the phase differs between viewers) | fx: transition, bits 0-2 effect (0 cut 1 fade 2 wipe right 3 wipe down 4 slide from right 5 slide from bottom 6 dissolve 7 iris), bit 3 hide (else show), bits 4-5 duration (0.25/0.5/1/2 s), bit 6 toggles to replay | cycle: palette cycling start<<4|length | timing: cycle steps/s<<4 | blink frequency in 0.5 Hz steps | blink_view: blink colour<<4 | zoom bits 0-1 (0 x1 1 x2 2 x4) | 4 mirror x | 8 mirror y | win_x / win_y: graphics window x0<<4|x1 in 16 screen px cells (inclusive) | sumG / sumT: 16-bit checksums (sum of the renderer's 16-bit words mod 65536, the two checksum words left out), written by the client once everything else has been sent; every viewer's shader sums its own copy and lights the status LED green when it matches (amber blinking: still arriving) | text_wrap_x / text_wrap_y: wrap period of the moving text in 8 px units (0 = the screen size, the old behaviour; else a glyph leaving one edge re-enters at the other, partly visible on both: smooth marquees of text longer than the screen) | text_move: 0 = every run moves with text_x / text_y and wraps on the whole screen; n > 0 = only runs n-1.. move, the vertical wrap counts from text_clip_y0 and they are clipped to the rows text_clip_y0 .. text_clip_y1 (0 = the bottom); the earlier runs stay put

sprites._doc: Hardware sprites, drawn by the text renderer (a renderer of their own would be one more material: PC Good allows 8, used: body 1 + sparkle 1 + display 5). Region = per sprite x, y, attr (3 B), then per sprite colours (2 B: palette index of pixel values 0-3, value 0 = transparent), then patterns (size x size, 2 bpp, rows MSB first). The registers come first, so moving a sprite changes one page. x / y = screen position + 32 (sprites can sit partly outside). attr: 1 visible, 2 flip x, 4 flip y, 8 double size, 16 above the text.

shapes._doc: Hardware shapes (vector layer, drawn by the text renderer from a shape table: the shader evaluates every shape per pixel, so moving / recolouring one = one page). 10 bytes per shape, 3 per page: b0 kind (low 4 bits: 0 none 1 line 2 rect 3 rrect 4 ellipse 5 arc 6 pie 7 tri 8 poly 9 bezier) | 16 fill | 32 above text | 64 xor (inverts what is under it) | 128 follows the graphics layer (offset + zoom); b1 fill colour << 4 | stroke colour; b2..b7 x0 y0 x1 y1 x2 y2 (screen px + offset; per kind some are raw parameters, see kd/shapes.py); b8 stroke width (bits 0-2) | pattern << 3 (0 solid 1 checker 2 h stripes 3 v stripes 4 diagonal 5 dots 6 h gradient 7 v gradient) | 64 round caps; b9 animation (bits 0-2: 0 none 1 rotate 2 pulse 3 blink 4 sweep) | signed 5-bit speed << 3. The region follows the sprites (page-aligned). Registers shape_x / shape_y (layer offset, wraps by each shape's anchor; shape_y sits in the first register page next to text_y, the old pad byte, so a text scroll and a shape scroll arrive in the same frame) and shape_vx / shape_vy (auto-scroll px/s).

anchor._doc: The anchor follows the head bone (smoothed by 'follow' per frame). The shader then offsets the screen centre in the avatar's own axes; all distances in metres relative to the head bone, measured on the avatar (2026-10-04). Side / front distances include half the screen width because the billboard turns to every viewer and sweeps that radius.

menu._doc: Expression menu (PC): buttons Top / Left / Right / Front -> pos_param (Int 0..3, LOCAL + saved); a local parameter driver copies it into the synced Bools pos_bits (bit 0, bit 1): 2 bits instead of 8. The size is register size (set by the client, Display.set(size_m=...)): 1..255 = size_min..size_max m, 0 = not set yet = screen.size_m.

commands._doc: Command frames: page ids above the memory pages that DO something on the avatar for a moment (an FX layer state entered while the id is on the wire); the payload is ignored. Every command (clear_gfx too) is allocated from 255 down, so the memory can grow upward without ever reaching them (memory pages 1..pages must stay below the lowest command id). Not seen by late joiners: one-shot effects only, states go in registers.

wings._doc: Two side screens (left / right wing), the size of the main screen, folded behind it like a satellite's solar arrays; register show bit 1 unfolds the left one, bit 2 the right one, each on its own (FX layers KD Wing L / KD Wing R play _KDWingL / _KDWingR 0 -> 1 over open_s, 1 -> 0 over close_s). No extra memory: content is ROUTED to a wing by registers that sit in the same register page as show (a late joiner gets routes and the device together, and they only change when the split changes): wing_tl / wing_tr = first text page (index in the text area) of the left / right wing's region (0 = none; the regions sit at the end of the text area, the main text before them), wing_gl / wing_gr = first graphics tile of the left / right wing's picture (0 = none; pictures on wings need the low-resolution mode, tiles placed like the main screen's), wing_shp = first shape slot of the left wing << 4 | first slot of the right wing (0 = none), wing_spr = 2 bits per sprite (0 main, 1 left, 2 right), wing_mv = page (from the region start) where each wing's MOVING text begins, left << 4 | right (0 = none): those runs move with the main screen's text registers (text_x/y, speeds, wrap, clip), so three chat logs scroll in step; wing_ly / wing_ry = a wing's own vertical offset for its moving text instead (0 = follow text_y / text_vy, n = offset n - 1, no auto-scroll): three logs that scroll on their own. wing_lsy / wing_rsy = the vertical offset of a wing's shapes (mod the screen height, like shape_y; FOLLOW shapes on a wing stay put). Wing content uses the wing's own screen coordinates (0..W, 0..H). At the side positions the device moves outward while the wings open (the inner wing never reaches the head).

show._doc: Appear / leave: register show (1 = shown), written by the client from Display.set(on=...); an FX layer watches that register byte while its page is on the wire and plays _KDShow 0 -> 1 over appear_s when it turns 1, 1 -> 0 over leave_s when 0; the shader pops the whole device in with an overshoot, then the screen opens from a line (CRT power-on); leaving runs it backwards. A late joiner / avatar reload gets it with the register refresh. (Was the synced Bool KD_On: a register costs no parameter bits.)

sound._doc: Notification sound on the avatar: command frame (page id = command, see commands) sent by Display.chime(); an FX layer plays the clip on the avatar's shared one-shot AudioSource when that id is on the wire. Everyone in earshot hears it once; a late joiner does not (a command is a moment, not a state). The clip is synthesized by build.py (two-note chime). (Was the synced Bool KD_Sfx.)
